target_customer: Marketing and SEO teams at brands and enterprises that want visibility in AI-generated answers
problem: Search is shifting from links to generative answers, and brands cannot see or influence whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude or Gemini cite or recommend them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, reported at about 295 to 499 USD per month entry pricing
product_category: Generative engine optimization and AI search visibility analytics

founders.name: Andrew Yan
prior_employers: Google Search (product manager, information acquisition team)
education: Columbia (degree not specified on YC page)

founders.name: Alan Yao
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a former jazz trombonist; employers and education not listed.

competitors.name: Profound
competitors.funding_then: 20M USD raised June 2025 per one roundup, unverified

competitors.what: Low-cost AI visibility tracker for small businesses
competitors.funding_then: 7M EUR raised July 2025 per one source, unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires querying many AI engines at scale, parsing citations and building analytics, which is standard engineering with some hard scaling and measurement problems; one source says the company was pre-product at raise.

defensibility.rationale: Many entrants launched in 2025 with similar tracking features and the data collection is replicable; some stickiness comes from historical visibility data and enterprise integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent SEO suites pushed back in 2025 with their own AI visibility features per one trade report. The YC page lists the company as acquired by Bloomreach, citing a Forbes headline, but this could not be corroborated.

market_need_then: In early 2025 marketers faced the shift from traditional search to AI-generated answers and had no tools to measure brand presence in them; a wave of funded GEO startups followed during 2025.

branding.domain_note: Uses athenahq.ai; exact domain history not found.

identity.logo: Wordmark AthenaHQ in site header; brand assets page exists
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and outcome-focused, headline Become the Brand AI Trusts.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder narratives such as the Whiplash band connection appear on the YC page; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is shared with athenahealth and many other Athena brands, making search confusion likely; named customers and Forbes and WSJ mentions on the site show decent reach but no brand-driven growth evidence.

outcome_analysis: AthenaHQ rode the 2025 shift to AI search, raising a seed of about 2.2M USD during its Winter 2025 batch and signing named enterprise logos. Founders came from Google Search and DeepMind, which fits the problem. The YC page now lists it as acquired by Bloomreach, but no independent source confirmed the deal, so the exit stays unknown here.
